description: Make real OAuth roles the primary authorization gate. Rewrite the staff guard to check the signed-in user's role (via the FEAT-001 session helpers) on the four staff mutation entry points, protect the /admin/* pages, wire Google sign-in/sign-out UI, link/create the Google user in the app_users table on first login (best-effort, only when DB configured), and deprecate the sessionStorage staff-token flow in the UI. Preserve the build-safety invariant (no env vars required for build) and the lazy DB pattern.
steps: Rewrite web/lib/auth/staff.ts so authorization is role-based via the FEAT-001 session helpers. authorizeStaff should now: if a signed-in staff user (isStaffRole) is present, allow; else reject with a Spanish error ('Debes iniciar sesión con una cuenta de personal autorizada para realizar esta operación.'). Reviewer-only vs admin-only distinctions: createCohort and saveAiConfig require SUPER_ADMIN or TEST_ADMIN; knowledge upload requires any staff role (SUPER_ADMIN/TEST_ADMIN/REPORT_REVIEWER); review PATCH requires REPORT_REVIEWER or SUPER_ADMIN. Keep STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN ONLY as an optional local/demo fallback: if isAuthConfigured() is false AND STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN is set, fall back to the legacy token check; if isAuthConfigured() is false AND STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN is unset, keep demo-mode open (so `next build` and local demos still work). Real OAuth roles are the primary gate whenever auth is configured. Preserve exports still used elsewhere (isStaffAuthEnabled, STAFF_TOKEN_HEADER, safeEqual behavior) or update all call sites accordingly.

Update web/lib/actions/cohorts.ts (createCohort) and web/lib/actions/ai-config.ts (saveAiConfig) to authorize via the new role-based check (SUPER_ADMIN/TEST_ADMIN). These are server actions so they read the session server-side; the staffToken arg becomes an optional legacy fallback only. Keep Spanish error messages.

Update web/app/api/knowledge/route.ts (POST) and web/app/api/sessions/[id]/review/route.ts (PATCH) to authorize via the new role-based check server-side (read the NextAuth session in the route handler). knowledge=any staff; review=REPORT_REVIEWER or SUPER_ADMIN. Return 401/403 with Spanish error when unauthorized.

Protect the /admin pages: in web/app/admin/page.tsx, web/app/admin/knowledge/page.tsx, web/app/admin/ai-settings/page.tsx, do a server-side session+role check (staff required). If not signed in or not staff, render a Spanish 'acceso restringido' state with a Google sign-in button/link (or redirect to sign-in). When auth is NOT configured, fall back to current behavior (show the page) so local/demo and the env-free build keep working. Prefer per-page server checks; a middleware.ts is optional but if added must not require env at build.

Add sign-in/sign-out UI. Create a small server or client component (Spanish labels: 'Iniciar sesión con Google', 'Cerrar sesión') that uses NextAuth signIn('google')/signOut. Wire it into web/app/layout.tsx topbar so the current user (email + role badge) and a sign-in/out control are visible. When auth is not configured, show a subtle 'Autenticación no configurada' note instead of a broken button.

On first successful Google login, link or create the user row in app_users (match by email; insert with resolved role, display_name from the Google profile name, auth_provider 'GOOGLE'). Do this best-effort ONLY when DATABASE_URL is configured, using query()/withTransaction() from web/lib/db.ts; wrap in try/catch so a missing/failing DB never blocks login. Put this in a signIn event/callback in the auth config or a helper invoked from it. Do NOT create the Pool at module load (preserve laziness).

Deprecate the sessionStorage staff-token flow in the UI: remove the StaffTokenField usage from web/components/AdminClient.tsx, web/components/KnowledgeAdminClient.tsx and web/components/AiSettingsClient.tsx and stop sending the x-staff-token header / staffToken arg from the client (rely on the server session instead). Replace the demo role-selector in AdminClient with the real signed-in user's identity/role from the session (passed down as a prop from the server page). You may keep web/components/StaffTokenField.tsx and web/components/useStaffToken.ts files in the repo but they must no longer be wired into the admin UI; if you keep them, add a deprecation comment. Keep everything Spanish.
acceptance_criteria: createCohort and saveAiConfig reject when the caller is not a signed-in SUPER_ADMIN/TEST_ADMIN (when auth is configured), returning a Spanish error.
POST /api/knowledge and PATCH /api/sessions/[id]/review reject non-staff (or wrong-role) callers with 401/403 and a Spanish error when auth is configured.
The /admin, /admin/knowledge and /admin/ai-settings pages show an 'acceso restringido' + Google sign-in state for non-staff/anonymous users when auth is configured.
The topbar shows a Google sign-in control when logged out and the user's identity + sign-out when logged in (or an 'Autenticación no configurada' note when unconfigured).
On first Google login with DATABASE_URL set, a matching row is created/linked in app_users (best-effort; failures do not block login).
StaffTokenField is no longer wired into the three admin client components; the demo role-selector in AdminClient is replaced by the real session identity.
With NO env vars set, `next build` still succeeds and the app runs in demo mode (admin pages accessible, mutations open) exactly as before.
`npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass.
verification: From web/: run `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` and confirm both pass.
From web/: run `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" npm run build` and confirm the build succeeds with no env vars.
From web/: run `npm run test -- --run` and confirm the suite passes (staff-auth tests are updated in FEAT-003).
